newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Austrian, Norwegian banks to issue Internet cash.
newsitem.headline: Austrian, Norwegian banks to issue Internet cash.

text.p: Den norske Bank, and Bank Austria, the largest banks in Norway and Austria, are to issue electronic cash developed by Dutch-based company DigiCash BV for use on the Internet, DigiCash said on Monday.

DigiCash said the banks would issue its "ecash" product which customers could use via a personal computer hooked up to the Internet for a range of products and services, including data base searches, news, entertainment and mail order products.
Ecash is said to allow secure payments over the Internet as sophisticated encryption techniques are used to encode electronic cash payments.
The payment system, unlike existing credit card payment facilities, allows for anonymous transactions as well as giving users the opportunity to make and receive payments.

"Ecash, like real cash, will allow consumers to shop in a secure and private manner which is both convenient and user friendly. These ecash implementations will significantly stimulate the electronic commerce markets in both Austria and Norway," DigiCash said.
Recent licensees of the DigiCash product, Deutsche Bank and Advance Bank of Australia, are now in the final stages of implementing "ecash" and will soon be issuing it to their clients, DigiCash said.
